newsitem.title: USA: American Express names Chenault COO.
newsitem.headline: American Express names Chenault COO.

text.p: American Express said Thursday it appointed Kenneth Chenault president and chief operating officer.
He had been a vice chairman and member of the Office of the Chief Executive since January 1995.
The position of president has been vacant since Jeff Stiefler resigned in September 1995.
Harvey Golub, chairman and chief executive, said in a statement that he plans to continue in his current position for another seven years, until he reaches 65.
He said today's announcement "clearly recognized" Chenault as the number-two executive in the company and the primary internal candidate to succeed him.

Golub said that as president and COO, all of the businesses will report to Chenault, effective immediately, with the exceptions of the American Express Financial Advisors and American Express Bank. Those two will report to Golub during a transition period, and then to Chenault.
He will also be responsible for Global Advertising and Brand Management and replace Golub as chief executive of travel-related services.

Chenault joined the company in 1981 as director of strategic planning. Golub said that since then, Chenault "provided strong leadership as we addressed a number of serious issues" that threatened the company's core card franchise.
